title: What Is a Black Hole?
summary: Find out why light cannot escape a black hole and how astronomers spot something they cannot see directly.
notes: Source: NASA Space Place, What Is a Black Hole? https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/black-holes/en/

steps.title: A boundary in space
sentences: Gravity is why planets orbit stars and why things fall to the ground.
A black hole is a region where gravity has shaped space so strongly that once anything crosses its boundary, it cannot get back out.
The boundary is called the event horizon. Even light cannot travel back out after crossing it.
points: Event horizon: the boundary beyond which light cannot return
The boundary is not a solid surface

steps.title: How a star can leave a black hole
sentences: A star's hot interior helps support it against gravity.
When some very massive stars run out of fuel, the core loses that support and collapses.
If enough mass is packed into a small enough space, a black hole can form.
points: Some massive stars collapse at the end of their lives
Not every star becomes a black hole

steps.title: Looking for clues
sentences: Imagine a visible star circling a point where you cannot see another star. Its motion tells you there is something massive pulling on it.
Gas can orbit a black hole, heat up and give off light or X-rays before falling in.
A bright ring in a black hole image shows hot material and bent light around a dark shadow.
points: Look for motion caused by an unseen mass
Light comes from material outside the event horizon

steps.title: Think like an astronomer
sentences: Imagine replacing a star with a black hole of exactly the same mass. A distant planet would still feel nearly the same gravitational pull.
The planet could keep its orbit, though it would lose the star's light and warmth.
A black hole does not behave like a vacuum cleaner that pulls everything nearby straight in.
points: Gravity depends on mass and distance
Objects can orbit a black hole without falling in

facts: The first image of a black hole shadow, in galaxy M87, was released in 2019.
Astronomers can also detect merging black holes by measuring ripples in space called gravitational waves.

quiz.q: If a beam of light has already crossed the event horizon, can it reach a telescope outside?
options: Yes, if the telescope is strong enough
No, light cannot escape once it crosses
quiz.why: The event horizon is the boundary beyond which no light can travel back out.

quiz.q: What could reveal a black hole even though it gives off no visible light of its own?
options: An ordinary cloud drifting near Earth
A shadow made by the Moon
A star orbiting a very massive unseen object
quiz.why: The star's motion is evidence of gravity from something we cannot see directly.

quiz.q: Why can a distant object stay in orbit around a black hole?
options: It can move sideways fast enough to keep missing the black hole
The black hole's gravity switches off at night
Space has a floor that holds it up
quiz.why: Like other orbits, it combines forward motion with gravity pulling inward.
